safety.name: Stop before actual transport start preserves unconsumed results
Batch membership freezes before a later arrival and duplicate finish cannot replay
Unknown transport outcome remains consumed and cannot restart the old input
A release cannot clear a live execution in B
A failed pause retry does not skip an independent release or settlement, and fresh B still submits
Persistent A prepare failure and broken diagnostics do not block B or its later Inbox input
A synchronous launch exception cannot strand the running latch or later Inbox input
Synchronous Stop persistence failure vetoes only its own input and a fresh B remains usable
A synchronous settlement construction failure retains its receipt without abandoning submitted work

expanded.system: Session Inbox delivery, admission, submission and continuation scheduling
expanded.proofScope: finite safety and weak-fairness temporal profiles

sqliteTimelines.bounds: Two explicit messages in one session, one preexisting and one future completion, one exact-ID Stop and duplicate, one lease-safe owner handoff; accept/begin/submit/settle/release A ordered; B, Stop and handoff interleave in all 336 possible orders. Late A release is also tried while future input owns slot. Injected synchronous provider-start boundary; no native process or lease producer.

sync-replay-current.limits: SQL transactions, gate class and the complete assistant-entry write method are production code. The late-writer witness uses a synthetic SQLite-backed history port and a diagnostic span stub; it does not test the real HistoryWriter. This is not end-to-end CRDT, RPC, permission, watcher, provider or UI acceptance. Accepted two-message events represent host admission after verified delivery, not arbitrary raw remote packets.

negativeAck.boundary: actual recovery and candidate selection; fresh-ID continuation and legacy-marker removal

decision-replay-current.limits: Unchanged source declaration spans are compiled with actual helper bodies. Synthetic workspace and session ports replace document I/O. Full watcher lifecycle, authorization, durable Inbox acceptance, actual Agent execution and UI are not executed. This checks recovery/selection and later fresh input, not full Agent execution or device acceptance.

expanded.limits: Finite slices, not a proof of full implementation composition. No actual Loro/Roost replication/reconnect, E2EE/revocation, host-lease producer, real provider, OS disk exhaustion or UI/device acceptance. Declarations and recovery/RPC-selection methods are compiled unchanged with actual policy helpers and synthetic document ports. The complete assistant-entry writer is also compiled unchanged; its tested existing-author branch uses a synthetic SQLite history port and a diagnostic span stub. This is a cancellation-fence witness, not full HistoryWriter acceptance. Host epochs assume an already-safe handoff. Per-ID receipts grow with failed identities; only the serialized host appends them. The default checks current finite temporal properties; source-only and safety-only cannot replace that result. Full workspace checks require dependencies absent from this nested checkout.

limits: Original scheduling slice is finite: two sessions, one retained A settlement, one B batch/input/Stop and at most two B starts; weak fairness and repeated wake opportunities, B never stopped in progress profile. Expanded slices and exact source limits are in expanded-coverage.json. Real replay uses production service/owner/repository/native SQLite, injected provider start and logger port. Native capacity fixture is not OS disk exhaustion. No full app/replication/authorization/native provider/device acceptance, unbounded refinement or whole-database-outage availability is proved. Current source changes are in the working tree, not implied by the base commit.
